text.p: The marriage of Swedish banks Swedbank and Foreningsbanken received the market's blessing on Tuesday as a boost to a banking sector which is in the throes of a major restructuring.
The new bank, ForeningsSparbanken, will be Sweden's second largest bank after the merger of Handelsbanken and Stadshypotek which was completed this week.

"The merger terms were pretty much in line with expectations and should boost Swedbank's share price," said analyst Jan Dworsky of Fiba. "Shareholders in Foreningsbanken should get the upside in Swedbank from the merger."
Swedbank, which is known as Sparbanken in Sweden, and Foreningsbanken jointly announced merger talks on Monday and trading in the banks' shares was suspended.

Swedbank, which has a market capitalisation of 30 billion crowns ($4 billion), jumped 20 crowns to 139.5 crowns when trading resumed on Tuesday. Foreningsbanken, capitalised at seven billion crowns, rose 4.70 to 43.20 crowns.

Under the terms of the agreement Swedbank will offer two shares in the new bank for every seven Foreningsbanken A shares. The cost of merging was expected not to exceed two billion crowns but the two banks expected to see savings of 1.5 billion crowns a year from 2000. Up to 2,000 of 13,000 staff will go.
The banks' main shareholders support the move which is conditional on 90 percent agreement from Foreningsbanken's shareholders.

"The boards think that a merger on an equal basis between Foreningsbanken and Swedbank is a logical and necessary step to create a long-term strong and efficient bank for the next century," the banks said in a statement.
"The stronger market position means that ForeningsSparbanken will have good growth opportunities."
The banks will publish a prospectus on April 11 with the offer period running to May 15.
The merger of the two banks which have a large retail customer base came as no surprise as Swedbank's interest in Foreningsbanken has been known since 1994.
Foreningsbanken, which has a strong rural customer base and is 20 percent owned by farmers' associations, spurned advances from Swedbank last June.
"The merger is seen as positive and in line with expectations but it was about three to four months earlier than we expected," said analyst Matthew Czepliewicz of Salomon Bros.
The merged bank will have combined assets of 657 billion crowns compared with Handelsbanken/Stadhypotek's 870 billion.
Swedbank and Foreningsbanken posted 1996 results on Tuesday.
Swedbank's result was better than expected with a 20 percent lift in operating profit to 5.30 billion crowns. The market had expected a profit of 4.99 billion crowns.
Foreningsbanken's result was in line with expectations with a 14 percent rise in operating profit to 1.16 billion crowns.

Analysts expected the merger to entice the last two of Sweden's four major banks not currently in a merger deal to re-think their plans. Merger talks between S-E-Banken and state-controlled Nordbanken collapsed two weeks ago.
"It will put more pressure on S-E-Banken to do something," said Dworsky.

Restructuring in Sweden's bank sector began last year as the sector, recovered from a property crisis in the early 1990s, started to prepare to compete against large, European rivals, building muscle through size and cutting costs.
